column3: “Any man” renders “a man, a man” (also in verses 8, 10 and 13), and “a lamb” renders “kesev,” a young ram.
“bloodguiltiness” renders “blood,” and “the tabernacle” renders “the dwelling place (mishkan).”
NASB supplies “The reason is”; “the open field” renders “the face of the field.”
“the goat demons” renders “se’irim,” goats (hairy ones), and “play the harlot” renders “prostitute themselves after.”
“its blood is identified with its life” interprets a difficult phrase, “its blood is in its life.”
